memory_bandwidth.notes: Working set: x (8*2048*4096*2B=128MB) + weight (4096*2B=8KB) + cos/sin (2048*64*4B=512KB). Output 128MB. Total ~256MB DRAM traffic if fully fused. Lower bound latency ~256e6/896e9 ≈ 0.286 ms.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Reading x twice (variance pass + apply) doubles read traffic unless we do single-pass with welford or just load-all-into-registers since head_dim*num_heads=4096 fits per row.

register_pressure.notes: Per (B,S) row we have 4096 fp16 = 8KB activations. BLOCK over D=4096 with one program per (B*S) row, load full row into shared/registers — feasible at BLOCK_D=4096.
register_pressure.risk: Holding 4096 fp16 in registers per program may spill; better to use shared memory or tile but recompute mean.

nodes.notes:
ANALYSIS:
1) Classification: fused elementwise + per-row reduction (RMSNorm) + elementwise gather (cos/sin) + pairwise rotation (RoPE). Memory bound.
2) Math: For each (b,s): var = mean(x^2), inv = rsqrt(var+eps); y = x*inv*w; then for each head h and pair i in [0,half): y1=y[2i], y2=y[half+i] (within head); out[..,i]=y1*cos[s,i]-y2*sin[s,i]; out[..,half+i]=y1*sin[s,i]+y2*cos[s,i]. cos/sin shape (S, head_dim/2) shared across batch & heads.
3) Layout: x (B,S,D) contiguous, D=4096; reshape to (B,S,H=32,Hd=128). RMSNorm reduces over D=4096. cos/sin (S,64) fp32 (from precompute, .half() doesn't convert buffers registered after? actually .half() converts module incl buffers -> cos/sin become fp16).
4) Regimes: (a) Large batch (current 8*2048=16384 rows): plenty of parallelism, BW-bound. (b) Small batch: latency-bound, want fewer kernel launches. (c) Very long seq: cos/sin reuse via L2.
5) Knobs: one program per row vs per (row, head); single-pass (compute sum of squares, then second pass over same row reloaded from regs/SMEM) vs two-pass; block size for D; whether to keep row in SMEM (8KB) or registers; vectorized loads (fp16x8); cos/sin cached in shared.
6) Skeleton: grid=(B*S,). Each program loads full row D=4096 fp16 into SMEM/registers using a loop with BLOCK=1024 or single BLOCK=4096. Compute sum of squares in fp32, rsqrt. Second loop: multiply by w and inv, then within each head, do RoPE using cos/sin loaded once per program (since same s). Store.
7) Families: (A) Single fused row-kernel holding row in registers/SMEM — TOP. (B) Two kernels: RMSNorm then RoPE — extra DRAM RT. (C) Per-(row,head) kernel with shared mean via atomics or 2-pass — complex.
Full-fusion is feasible: 8KB row fits easily in SMEM (128KB/SM). Top candidate is single fused kernel.
SELF_CHECK n/a (root).

action.description: Single Triton kernel with grid=(B*S,). Each program loads the entire D=4096 fp16 row into shared memory, computes sum-of-squares in fp32, rsqrt, then applies weight and RoPE rotation per-head using cos/sin loaded once per row. Store result. Use BLOCK_D=4096 (constexpr) or tiled with two passes if register pressure too high.
action.rationale: Reads x once, writes out once; minimal global traffic ~256MB, near peak BW. Avoids torch.compile's likely 2-kernel split (norm then rope) and extra cat allocation.

Tactic: each program handles ROWS_PER_PROG rows (e.g. 2-4), reusing cos/sin loads for the same seq positions when grouped by s, and reducing the number of programs (B*S/ROWS_PER_PROG). Reduces launch/scheduling overhead and increases per-program arithmetic intensity. Risk: register pressure since each row has 4096 fp16 elements; may need to keep rows small. Expected: small but real gain over 1.34x.

kernel_summary: Fused RMSNorm + Rotary Position Embedding on fp16 (B=8,S=2048,D=4096,H=32,Hd=128). Per row (b,s): compute mean(x^2) over D, rsqrt, multiply by learnable weight, reshape to heads, apply rotate_half RoPE using precomputed cos/sin of shape (S, Hd/2). Memory-bound: ~256MB of essential DRAM traffic; lower bound ~0.29ms at 896GB/s. Key constraints: row size 8KB fits easily in SMEM; cos/sin shared across batch and heads (only 64 values per s); want single fused kernel to avoid intermediate writeback that torch.compile likely does.

Single-pass keep-row-in-registers vs two-pass reload (reload from global vs from shared) — which wins on RTX5090M?
Is the output layout after reshape((B,S,D)) bit-identical to writing in head-major order? (Yes since head_dim contiguous segments concatenate to D.)
Does the reference's torch.cat along last dim produce [first half rotated, second half rotated] per head? confirmed — must store into [..., :half] and [..., half:] of each head's slice.
